_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: render indices 2, 4, 6 (= printed Page 3, 5, 7 of 7). PAGE MAP, every one of the 7 indices accounted for: idx 0 = bilingual cover (printed Page 1, Set No. 3, Q.P. Code 65/2/3, 'contains 14 questions', Time 2 hours / Max Marks 40); idx 1 = HINDI General Instructions + Hindi Q1-Q5 (Page 2); idx 2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + English SECTION A header + Q1-Q5 (Page 3); idx 3 = HINDI Q6 + Section B header + Q7-Q10 (Page 4); idx 4 = ENGLISH Q6 + SECTION B header + Q7-Q10 (Page 5); idx 5 = HINDI Section C header + Q11-Q14 (Page 6); idx 6 = ENGLISH SECTION C header + Q11-Q14 (Page 7). The 'even indices are English' hypothesis HELD exactly, and all three of the brief's known failure modes were checked individually and are ABSENT: (1) NO odd page carries any English overflow - idx 1 opens with the Hindi 'सामान्य निर्देश' block, idx 3 with Hindi Q6 (क), idx 5 with the Hindi 'खण्ड ग' header, each verified on the full-size render, because this paper breaks its language blocks cleanly on page boundaries (idx 2 ends at Q5, idx 4 opens at Q6; idx 4 ends at Q10, idx 6 opens at Q11); (2) there is NO English-only final page - idx 6 is the ordinary even English page; (3) there is NO parity inversion - each language uses exactly 3 content pages. Cover states 7 printed pages and the last folio reads 'Page 7 of 7' - they agree. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so per the brief the count was established by WALKING THE OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question (ms idx 2-10, which reprints both branches under '6.(a) ... Or ... 6.(b)'). FOUR internal choices: Q6, Q7, Q8, Q12 - each printed as (a) OR (b), all four confirmed in the scheme. Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13 carry NO alternative (single undivided block in both the paper and the scheme). Q14's (a)/(b) are case-study SUB-PARTS, not an internal choice - both compulsory, 2 marks each. Marks check on primary branches: Section A 6x2 = 12, Section B 4x3 = 12, Section C 3x4 + Q14 (2+2) = 16, total 40 - consistent, though per the brief this sum is structurally blind to a dropped ALTERNATIVE and is NOT what established the count. NO MCQs anywhere - all 14 questions are subjective, so 'format' is 'subjective' on all 19 rows and there is no key to re-derive. OVERLAP WITH 65/2/1, judged by CONTENT and not by plan.txt: this set is a RESHUFFLE of 65/2/1, and 14 of the 19 rows are word-for-word the reference's (my Q1=ref Q6, Q2=ref Q5, Q3=ref Q4, Q4=ref Q3, Q5=ref Q1, Q7a=ref Q8a, Q7b=ref Q8b, Q8a=ref Q10a, Q8b=ref Q10b, Q11=ref Q12, Q12a=ref Q13a, Q12b=ref Q13b, Q14a=ref Q14a, Q14b=ref Q14b). Each was read on MY page first and only then copied from the reference file byte-for-byte, per the brief's recommended method, so they dedup at commit. GENUINELY NEW, 5 rows: Q6a, Q6b, Q9, Q10, Q13. plan.txt's headline count (5 new) happens to agree, but its per-question labels do not describe the paper's own numbering at all - it names Q1#1, Q2#1, Q4#1, Q5#2/#3, Q11#1/#2, Q14#1 as skips, whereas by content the shared questions are Q1-Q5, Q7, Q8, Q11, Q12 and Q14 and the new ones are Q6, Q9, Q10, Q13. Nothing was skipped: the whole paper is transcribed. NO printing defect found in the question paper - every stem is clean, well-posed and internally consistent (checked: Q4's |2a+3b|=|3a-2b| gives a.b=0; Q9 is genuinely homogeneous and integrates to xe^(y/x)+y=C; Q10 is solvable only because a.b = 2+1-3 = 0, which it is). No _figure is REQUIRED anywhere; the only image in the paper is Q14's decorative cricket coin-toss clip-art.

questions.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
questions.stem: Write the cartesian equation of the line PQ passing through points \( P(2, 2, 1) \) and \( Q(5, 1, -2) \). Hence, find the y-coordinate of the point on the line PQ whose z-coordinate is \( -2 \).

Probabilities of A and B solving a specific problem are \( \frac{2}{3} \) and \( \frac{3}{5} \), respectively. If both of them try independently to solve the problem, then find the probability that the problem is solved.
A pair of dice is thrown. It is given that the sum of numbers appearing on both dice is an even number. Find the probability that the number appearing on at least one die is 3.
\( \vec{a} \) and \( \vec{b} \) are two unit vectors such that \( |2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}| = |3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| \). Find the angle between \( \vec{a} \) and \( \vec{b} \).

questions.subtopic: Order and Degree of a Differential Equation
questions.stem: Find the product of the order and the degree of the differential equation \( \left[ \frac{d}{dx} (xy^2) \right] \cdot \frac{dy}{dx} + y = 0 \).
Find the equation of the plane passing through points \( (2, 1, 0) \), \( (3, -2, -2) \) and \( (1, 1, -7) \). Also, obtain its distance from the origin.
Find the distance between the lines \( x = \frac{y - 1}{2} = \frac{z - 2}{3} \) and \( x + 1 = \frac{y + 2}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{3} \).
Solve the following differential equation : \( (1 + e^{y/x}) \, dy + e^{y/x} \left( 1 - \frac{y}{x} \right) dx = 0 \)

If \( \vec{a} \) and \( \vec{b} \) are two vectors such that \( \vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} \) and \( \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 3\hat{k} \), then find the vector \( \vec{c} \), given that \( \vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b} \) and \( \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 4 \).

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the smaller region enclosed by the curve \( 4x^2 + 4y^2 = 9 \) and the line \( 2x + 2y = 3 \).

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: If the area of the region bounded by the curve \( y^2 = 4ax \) and the line \( x = 4a \) is \( \frac{256}{3} \) sq. units, then using integration, find the value of a, where \( a > 0 \).

questions.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the point where the line through \( (5, 1, 6) \) and \( (3, 4, 1) \) crosses the zx-plane.

questions.context:
At the start of a cricket match, a coin is tossed and the team winning the toss has the opportunity to choose to bat or bowl. Such a coin is unbiased with equal probabilities of getting head and tail.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: If such a coin is tossed 2 times, then find the probability distribution of number of tails.
